source_text: Nec putem disceptandum, an digne Deus prohibeat nomen et honorem suum mendacio addici, an digne quos ab errore superstitionis avulserit, rursus in Aegyptum regredi nolit; an digne a se non patitur absistere quos sibi allegit. Itaque nec illud exspectabit retractari a nobis, an observari voluerit disciplinam quam voluit instituere, et an merito ulciscatur desertam, quam voluit observatam: quando frustra instituisset, si observari eam noluisset; et frustra observari voluisset, si vindicare noluisset. Sequitur enim ut has definitiones Dei adversus superstitiones, tam evictas quam etiam vindicatas probem, quoniam ex his tota martyriorum ratio constabit. Aberat apud Deum in monte Moyses, cum populus tam necessariam absentiam ejus impatiens, deos sibi producere quaerit, quos potius ipse perdiderit. Urgetur Aaron, et jubet inaures foeminarum suarum in ignem conferri. Amissuri enim erant in judicium sibi vera ornamenta aurium, Dei voces. Sapiens ignis effigiem vituli defundit illis, suggillans illic cor habentes, ubi et thesaurum, apud Aegyptum scilicet inter caetera animalia bovis etiam cujusdam consecratricem; itaque tria millia hominum a parentibus proximis caesa, quia tam proximum parentem Deum offenderant, transgressionis et primordia et merita dedicaverunt. In Arithmis, cum divertisset Israel apud Sethim, abeunt libidinatum ad filias Moab, invitantur ad idola, ut et spiritu fornicarentur; edunt denique de pollutis eorum: dehinc et adorant deos gentis, et Beelphegor initiantur. Ob hanc quoque idololatriam, moechiae sororem, viginti tria millia domesticis obtruncata gladiis divinae irae litaverunt. Defuncto Jesu Nave, derelinquunt Deum patrum suorum, et serviunt idolis Baalim et Astartis; et iratus Dominus tradidit eos in manibus diripientium; et diripiebantur ab illis, et venundabantur inimicis, nec poterant omnino subsistere a facie inimicorum suorum; quocumque processerant, manus erat super illos in mala, et compressati sunt valde. Post quae instituit super illos Deus Critas, quos censores intelligimus, sed nec istis obaudire perseverarunt: ut quis Critarum obierat, illi ad delinquendum supra quam patres eorum, abeundo post deos alienorum et serviendo et adorando eos. Itaque Dominus iratus: Quoniam quidem, ait, transgressa est gens ista pactum meum, quod disposui patribus eorum, et non audierunt vocem meam, et ego non advertam ad auferendum virum a facie eorum ex nationibus quas relinquit decedens Jesu. Atque ita per omnes pene annales critarum et deinceps regum, reservatis gentium circumcolarum viribus, bello et captivitate et jugo allophylorum iram dispensavit Israel, quotienscumque ab illo maxime in idololatriam exorbitaverunt.
pass_a_gloss: Nor do I think it is to be disputed, whether God rightly prohibits His name and honor from being added to a lie, whether He rightly does not allow those whom He has torn away from the error of superstition to return again to Egypt, whether He rightly does not permit those whom He has chosen for Himself to depart from Him. Therefore, He will not wait for us to retract whether He wanted to observe the discipline which He wanted to establish, and whether He rightly avenges the deserted discipline which He wanted to be observed: for He would have established it in vain if He did not want it to be observed; and He would have wanted it to be observed in vain if He did not want to avenge it. For it follows that I prove these definitions of God against superstitions, both those that have been overcome and those that have been avenged, since from these the entire reason for martyrdom will consist. Moses was absent with God on the mountain, when the people, impatient of his necessary absence, sought to produce gods for themselves, which they had rather lost. Aaron was urged on, and ordered the earrings of their women to be cast into the fire. For they were about to lose in judgment the true ornaments of their ears, the voices of God. The wise fire poured out a calf's image for them, bruising those who had hearts, where also the treasure, namely among the other animals of Egypt, even a certain consecrator of the cow; and so three thousand men were slain by their nearest relatives, because they had offended the nearest parent, God, and they dedicated the beginnings and merits of the transgression. In Arithmus, when Israel had turned aside at Sethim, they went to the daughters of Moab, having been invited to idols, so that they might also fornicate in spirit; they ate finally of their polluted things: then they also worshiped the gods of the nation, and were initiated into Beelphegor. On account of this idolatry also, the sister of fornication, twenty-three thousand of the domestic were slain by the swords of divine wrath. After Jesus Nave died, they abandoned the God of their fathers, and served the idols Baalim and Astartis; and the Lord, being angry, delivered them into the hands of those who plundered them; and they were plundered by them, and sold to their enemies, nor could they at all stand before the face of their enemies; wherever they went, the hand was upon them in evil, and they were greatly oppressed. After these things, God established the Critics over them, whom we understand to be censors, but they did not obey even these: so that when one of the Critics died, they went to sin beyond what their fathers had done, going after the gods of foreigners and serving and worshiping them. And so the Lord, being angry, said: 'Since this nation has transgressed my covenant, which I established with their fathers, and they have not listened to my voice, I will not turn to take away the man from before their face from the nations which remain when Jesus departs.' And so, throughout almost all the annals of the Critics and afterwards of the kings, with the forces of the surrounding nations reserved, He dispensed His wrath to Israel in war and captivity and the yoke of foreigners, as often as they greatly deviated into idolatry from Him.

pass_b_english: I do not think it is even debatable whether God is right to forbid His name and honor from being attached to a lie, whether He is right to refuse those He has torn from the error of superstition permission to return to Egypt, or whether He is right to refuse those He has chosen for Himself permission to depart from Him. (Exodus 32:1-6) Consequently, He will not wait for us to re-examine whether He intended to enforce the discipline He chose to establish, and whether He justly punishes the abandonment of that discipline which He intended to be kept. He would have established it in vain if He did not want it kept, and He would have wanted it kept in vain if He did not intend to punish its violation. It follows, then, that I must prove these definitions of God against superstitions—both those already refuted and those already punished—because the entire rationale for martyrdom rests on them.

Moses was absent with God on the mountain when the people, unable to endure his necessary absence, demanded gods for themselves—gods they had already lost. Aaron was pressed into compliance and ordered the women's earrings thrown into the fire. They were about to forfeit in judgment the true ornaments of their ears: the very voices of God. A shrewd fire cast a calf's image for them, branding those who had hearts set on Egypt, where even a cow was consecrated among the other animals. As a result, three thousand men were slain by their own kin, because they had offended their nearest parent, God, thereby consecrating the origin and the penalty of their transgression. (Exodus 32:1-6)

In Numbers, when Israel encamped at Shittim, the men went whoring after the daughters of Moab, who invited them to their idols so that they would commit spiritual fornication as well. They ate the sacrifices of those polluted rites, then bowed down to the gods of the nation and were initiated into Baal-peor. On account of this idolatry, fornication's sister, twenty-three thousand Israelites fell by the swords of divine wrath. (Numbers 25:1-9)

After Joshua died, they abandoned the God of their fathers and served the idols Baal and Ashtoreth. The Lord burned with anger, handed them over to plunderers, and they were plundered and sold to enemies against whom they could no longer stand. Wherever they marched, the Lord's hand was against them for disaster, and they were severely crushed. (Judges 2:10-15) After this, God raised up Judges—whom we understand as censors—over them, but they would not obey even these. Whenever a Judge died, they reverted to corruption worse than their fathers, chasing after foreign gods, serving and worshiping them. So the Lord grew angry and declared: 'Because this nation has transgressed My covenant which I commanded their fathers, and has not obeyed My voice, I will no longer drive out before them any of the nations Joshua left when he died.' (Judges 2:10-15) Thus, throughout nearly all the annals of the Judges and the subsequent kings, with the strength of the surrounding nations held in reserve, He meted out His wrath to Israel through war, captivity, and the yoke of foreigners, every time they strayed far into idolatry.

review.notes: Pass A and Pass B both correctly handle the complex Latin syntax. Pass B provides necessary scripture citations (Exodus 32:1-6, Numbers 25:1-9, Judges 2:10-15) which are required for the allusions present in the text. Pass B correctly identifies 'Critas' as 'Judges' in the context of the biblical narrative, whereas Pass A leaves it as 'Critics', but Pass B's translation is more faithful to the intended meaning of the historical/biblical context described. The translation of 'suggillans' as 'branding' (B) vs 'bruising' (A) is a matter of interpretation of the Latin, but both are acceptable. The translation of 'Beelphegor' (Latin) to 'Baal-peor' (B) is a correct identification of the biblical figure.
